meta.title: A Bottle with a Paw Print

paragraphs: On Saturday afternoon, Tom and Lily went to a small shop near the bus stop. Tom had a school camp next week, and he needed a hat and a bottle. Dad gave him some money, two hundred baht. Lily came to help him. The shop was very tidy. Several hats were on the wall, and the bottles stood in a row on a shelf.

"Good afternoon," said the man at the desk. "Can I help you?" "How much is this blue hat?" asked Tom. "It is eighty baht," said the man. Tom put the hat on his head, and it looked good. "And how much is this green bottle?" "That one is one hundred and twenty baht." "Then I can buy both," said Tom. "The price is two hundred baht."

Lily looked at a high shelf. "Look, Tom!" she said. "There is an unusual bottle up there." It was white, and it had a green flag with a paw print. "That is the Explorers' sign!" said Tom. "How much is it?" The man took it down. "It is one hundred and fifty baht," he said. "The hat and this bottle are two hundred and thirty baht," said Tom. "But I have only two hundred."

Lily took some money from her pocket. "I have thirty baht," she said. "I hope that helps." "It is just right," said the man. "If you buy two things, the bag is free." Tom paid, and the man put the hat and the white bottle in a bag. "Where is the bus stop, please?" asked Lily. "Turn left," said the man. "It is in front of the bank."

The bus came at a quarter past four. Tom looked at the bottle on the bus. "Thank you, Lily," he said. "You are a good sister." "You can show it at camp," said Lily. "Then everyone can see our club sign." Tom smiled and held the bag on his knees.
